meta.title: Quantum Circuits and Entanglement
meta.subtitle: Controlled gates, Bell states, and circuit depth

slides.title: Circuit model
body: A circuit is a sequence of gates on wires (qubits).
Time flows left to right.
Each gate is a matrix applied to the state.
Why circuits: they let us compose many linear operations into one unitary.

slides.title: Circuit notation
body: Each horizontal line is a qubit wire.
Boxes are gates; dots and lines indicate control.
Measurement is drawn with a meter symbol and produces classical bits.
Why the diagram works: it mirrors matrix multiplication order.

slides.title: Single-qubit layers
body: Layers apply gates in parallel on different qubits.
Depth measures the number of sequential layers.
Reducing depth can reduce error and decoherence.
Why depth matters: real devices have short coherence times.

slides.title: Controlled gates
body: A controlled gate applies an operation if the control is 1.
The most common is CNOT: $$|a,b\rangle \to |a, b \oplus a\rangle$$
Why control is powerful: it creates correlations between qubits.

quiz.question: With the first qubit as control, what is CNOT applied to $|1,0\rangle$?
quiz.explain: Control is 1, so the target bit flips to 1.

slides.title: Bell state
body: Create entanglement with H and CNOT:
1) Apply H to the first qubit.
2) Apply CNOT with the first as control.
Result: $$|\Phi^+\rangle = (|00\rangle + |11\rangle)/\sqrt{2}$$
Why it is special: this state cannot be written as a product of two single-qubit states.

check.prompt: Check: Start with $|00\rangle$, apply H on qubit 1 then CNOT ($1 \to 2$). What state do you get?
check.explain: Correct - the circuit prepares an entangled Bell pair.

slides.title: Measurement in circuits
body: Measurement collapses qubits to classical bits.
Measurements can be placed at the end or mid-circuit.
Repeated runs estimate probabilities and expectation values.
Why measurement changes things: it is not unitary and discards phase information.

slides.title: Circuit depth and width
body: Width is the number of qubits used.
Depth is the number of sequential gate layers.
Hardware limits often cap depth more than width.
Why: noise accumulates with each layer.

slides.title: Swap and controlled-Z
body: SWAP exchanges two qubits and can be built from 3 CNOTs.
Controlled-Z flips the phase when both qubits are 1.
Both are common building blocks in larger circuits.
Why use them: hardware connectivity often forces explicit swaps or phase controls.

slides.title: Composing larger circuits
body: Large circuits are built from small reusable blocks.
Common patterns: prepare $\to$ compute $\to$ uncompute.
This keeps extra qubits clean and reduces error.
Why uncompute: it removes unwanted entanglement and resets ancilla qubits.

check.explain: Correct - it is entangled and not separable.
